name: gh-pr
description: GitHub commit-to-merge lifecycle: commit, open a PR, second-opinion AI review, per-comment replies, approve, merge, audited emergency override, serial merge train.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the gh-pr skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Search contents with `Grep`; match paths with `Glob`. Every skill here drives the `gh` CLI and `git` -- run them with `Bash` and pass the output through verbatim.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`. `gh-pr:approve` and `gh-pr:review` use one for a large diff; without it, read the diff inline -- a slower route to the same verdict, not a reduced one.
- Claude Code's `Skill` tool has no Kimi equivalent. `gh-pr:merge-train` chains the other skills through it; without a skill-invocation tool, run the per-PR skills directly -- `gh-resolve:outdated` / `:conflict` / `:ci-fail`, then `gh-pr:merge` -- one PR at a time.
- All eight need an authenticated `gh` CLI and carry `GH_HOST` plus `--repo` on every call, because `--repo` alone names no server.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skills, not advice:

- `gh-pr:commit` commits only. It never pushes and never opens a PR -- that is `gh-pr:create`.
- `gh-pr:create` bundles every commit since the branch diverged from base, not just HEAD, and creates the PR only: no review, no merge.
- `gh-pr:review` never submits `--approve` or `--request-changes` and never replies to individual comments. It posts one aggregate comment.
- `gh-pr:reply` replies per comment, bots included, rather than summarising. It applies the fixes that hold up and says so on the ones it rejects.
- `gh-pr:approve` can never approve a PR authored by the same user. Blockers become `request changes`; the rest become follow-up issues.
- `gh-pr:merge` refuses an un-approved PR, failing CI, a draft, or a conflicted branch, and never swaps merge strategy when the chosen one fails.
- `gh-pr:merge-emergency` is the only bypass of that approval gate. It requires a written reason and files a follow-up incident issue; CI still gates.
- `gh-pr:merge-train` handles one PR at a time and never merges a PR the per-PR gates would have refused.

interface.longDescription: gh-pr bundles the eight commit-to-merge skills: commit, create, review, reply, approve, merge, merge-emergency, and merge-train.
